title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self: Misuse of Human Faculties and Their 2 Main Purposes

questions.question: How did the sinful group react to the signs that point to Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: They rejected them and chose disbelief.

questions.question: How did they behave toward the blessings around them?
questions.answer: They were ungrateful instead of thankful.

questions.question: What wrong attitude did they show toward creatures?
questions.answer: They treated them as worthless and insulted them.

questions.question: Why is their crime described as extremely great?
questions.answer: Because they denied many signs of Allah and rejected His names in a short life.

questions.question: What did they become deserving of because of this?
questions.answer: Endless punishment.

questions.question: According to the passage, why were life and human abilities given to people?
questions.answer: They were given so people could do the duties Allah intended.

questions.question: What mistaken idea about life does the passage warn against?
questions.answer: Thinking life is only for comfort, civilization, and feeding bodily desires.

questions.question: Are a person’s senses and body parts meant only for short worldly pleasures?
questions.answer: No. They were made for much higher purposes.

questions.question: What is the first main purpose of the human faculties?
questions.answer: To help a person recognize Allah’s blessings and thank and worship Him.

questions.question: What is the second main purpose of the human faculties?
questions.answer: To help a person notice the signs of Allah’s names in the world, experience them, and come to belief.

questions.question: How does a person become a real human being in this passage?
questions.answer: By reaching those two main goals.

questions.question: What happens to a person who fulfills these two goals?
questions.answer: The person grows and becomes complete in a true human way.

questions.question: When the wrongdoers reached the age of understanding, what path did they choose?
questions.answer: They chose unbelief and wrongdoing.

questions.question: Besides disbelief, what other sin did they show toward blessings?
questions.answer: They showed ingratitude.

questions.question: What did their disrespect toward creatures show about their belief?
questions.answer: It showed a faithless and insulting attitude.

questions.question: What did they deny besides the signs of unity?
questions.answer: They denied the displays of Allah’s beautiful names.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the result of denying these truths?
questions.answer: It says they committed a huge crime and deserved never-ending punishment.

questions.question: What question is asked to correct the idea that life is only for enjoying worldly comfort?
questions.answer: It asks whether life’s duty is just to live comfortably and satisfy physical cravings.

questions.question: What kinds of human abilities are listed as too noble for low desires alone?
questions.answer: The senses, feelings, faculties, organs, and body systems.

questions.question: What does “Allah forbid” show about the idea that humans were made only for desires?
questions.answer: It shows that idea is strongly rejected.

questions.question: What does the first purpose teach a person to notice?
questions.answer: The many gifts of the True Giver.

questions.question: After noticing those gifts, what should a person do?
questions.answer: Offer thanks and worship Allah.

questions.question: What does the second purpose help a person learn through the world?
questions.answer: It helps a person learn about the manifestations of Allah’s sacred names.

questions.question: After experiencing these signs, what should a person reach?
questions.answer: Real belief and recognition.

questions.question: What is the final result of living by these two purposes?
questions.answer: A person matures and becomes a true human being.

questions.question: Which two bad responses are mentioned first about the sinful group?
questions.answer: Disbelief toward the signs and ingratitude toward blessings.

questions.question: How did they treat the creatures of the world in their false view?
questions.answer: They looked down on them and dishonored them.

questions.question: What made their wrongdoing “boundless” in the passage?
questions.answer: They rejected the divine names and many proofs connected to them.

questions.question: Why does the passage say humans cannot use life any way they want?
questions.answer: Because life and human powers were given for special duties.

questions.question: What worldly view of life is being challenged?
questions.answer: The view that life is mainly about comfort and bodily enjoyment.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention delicate senses and well-made body systems?
questions.answer: To show they were created with wise and high purposes.

questions.question: What is one main reason humans were given these abilities?
questions.answer: So they can recognize Allah’s favors.

questions.question: What should come after recognizing Allah’s favors?
questions.answer: Gratitude and worship.

questions.question: What is the other main reason humans were given these abilities?
questions.answer: So they can notice and experience the signs of Allah’s names in creation.

questions.question: How does experience help a person according to the passage?
questions.answer: It helps the person know these signs and believe in them.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with true human growth?
questions.answer: Achieving the two main aims.

questions.question: What is the difference between the sinful group and the rightly guided person in this passage?
questions.answer: The sinful group wastes life by denial and ingratitude, while the rightly guided person uses life for thankfulness, worship, and belief.

questions.question: What happened when the wicked entered worldly life with enough understanding to choose?
questions.answer: They answered truth with unbelief.

questions.question: What should they have done with blessings, and what did they do instead?
questions.answer: They should have been thankful, but instead they were ungrateful.

questions.question: How did their unbelief affect the way they looked at creation?
questions.answer: They saw creatures as pointless and treated them disrespectfully.

questions.question: What does the passage say they denied about Allah?
questions.answer: They denied the ways His names appear in the world.

questions.question: What punishment did their actions make them deserve?
questions.answer: Everlasting punishment.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was the purpose of the “capital” of life?
questions.answer: It was meant for carrying out human duties.

questions.question: What false goal for life is criticized in the questions to the nafs?
questions.answer: Making life all about comfort and satisfying the body.

questions.question: Why are human faculties described as delicate, subtle, and curious?
questions.answer: To show they are too valuable to be used only for low desires.

questions.question: What is the first of the two main aims in human creation?
questions.answer: To know Allah’s gifts and respond with thanks.

questions.question: What acts are linked to that first aim?
questions.answer: Thankfulness and worship.

questions.question: What is the second main aim in human creation?
questions.answer: To know the manifestations of Allah’s names through one’s faculties and experience.

questions.question: What should happen in a person after recognizing these manifestations?
questions.answer: The person should come to faith.

questions.question: How does the passage define becoming fully human?
questions.answer: It means developing and becoming complete by fulfilling those two aims.

questions.question: In the passage, what three wrong attitudes describe the sinners and wicked?
questions.answer: Disbelief, ingratitude, and insulting creation.

questions.question: Why was insulting creatures also a serious spiritual wrong?
questions.answer: Because it came from denying their value as signs and works of Allah.

questions.question: What did they reject that made their guilt even greater?
questions.answer: The manifestations of the divine names.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the abilities given to humans?
questions.answer: They are a trust given for important duties.

questions.question: What everyday misunderstanding about life does the speaker challenge?
questions.answer: The idea that life is just for living comfortably and pleasing the body.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the senses and feelings are not for fleeting life alone?
questions.answer: Because they were created for lasting and meaningful purposes.

questions.question: What is the first great purpose of human abilities?
questions.answer: To recognize the many blessings from Allah.

questions.question: What should recognizing blessings lead a believer to do?
questions.answer: Thank and worship Allah.

questions.question: What is the second great purpose of human abilities?
questions.answer: To perceive how Allah’s names appear in the world.

questions.question: What should a person gain after perceiving those signs?
questions.answer: Faith through recognizing and experiencing them.

questions.question: What two outcomes come from fulfilling both purposes?
questions.answer: Human growth and true human completion.

questions.question: What did the wicked choose when they became old enough to understand responsibility?
questions.answer: They chose unbelief.

questions.question: How did they respond to the gifts they had been given?
questions.answer: They met them with thanklessness.

questions.question: What was their attitude toward the beings around them?
questions.answer: They acted as if those beings had no worth.

questions.question: What did they deny about Allah’s signs in the world?
questions.answer: They denied the ways His names are shown in creation.

questions.question: Why does the passage say they deserved endless punishment?
questions.answer: Because they used a short life to commit a very great denial.

questions.question: What had been given to human beings for better use than this?
questions.answer: Life and human faculties.

questions.question: What question is raised about civilization and bodily pleasure?
questions.answer: Whether these can really be the whole duty of life.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the purpose of human senses and organs?
questions.answer: They were not made only for worldly cravings.

questions.question: Name one of the two main aims of creating these faculties.
questions.answer: One aim is to let people know Allah’s blessings and thank Him.

questions.question: Name the other main aim of creating these faculties.
questions.answer: The other aim is to let people know the manifestations of Allah’s names and believe through that knowledge.

questions.question: What role does experience have in the second aim?
questions.answer: It helps a person recognize those manifestations in a real way.

questions.question: According to the last lines, what makes a person a true human being?
questions.answer: Fulfilling both main aims and growing through them.
